reviews.text: My 13-year-old rabbit had been chewing and seemed unable to eat since the day before yesterday, so I brought her in for the first time. They trimmed her teeth, and she was able to eat vegetables as soon as we got home.

My rabbit, who will soon be 9 years old, is a patient here.

I've seen two different veterinarians, and I thought both were excellent.

Although one veterinarian has received negative reviews in the past, I felt that he had a deep love for rabbits and was being strict out of genuine concern for their well-being. Following his advice, my rabbit's condition improved.

My rabbit is quite elderly and requires frequent vet visits, but I've decided to continue using this hospital.

For about two and a half years, they have been involved in our rabbit's regular checkups and treatment for stasis.

Three doctors and staff members have assisted us, and all of them were very kind and always put our rabbit's well-being first. Their straightforwardness in telling us what is good and what is bad is also very reassuring. Watching how they handled our rabbit during examinations, I always felt their skill and deep affection. I am so glad that this hospital is our rabbit's primary veterinarian. Although we are currently without a rabbit, we would like to continue using their services when we welcome another rabbit into our home.

Thank you so much for teaching me so much about rabbits. I also appreciate you explaining about my own rabbit; it helped me understand things better.

The pricing was clear and easy to understand.

From now on, I'll take my rabbit to the vet sooner if it gets sick.

A clinic overflowing with love for rabbits.

I regret not going here from the beginning.

The doctor who treated my rabbit probably had a bad reputation online, but he honestly explained both the good and bad aspects, and I personally found him to be a very trustworthy doctor.

I think he would be strict with people who keep their rabbits unclean or carelessly, out of concern for the poor rabbits.

His genuine dedication to rabbits is evident.

I will definitely be using his services again.

Thank you very much.

I'm not very good at explaining things, but please listen...

My first rabbit was taken care of here!

I adopted her when she was two months old, and took her to Saito Rabbit Clinic in Tabata, Kita-ku, which I heard about from the pet shop, for her first health checkup!

(This was in November 2010)

At the clinic, Dr. Fukumura gave me detailed advice, such as, "Feed your rabbit mainly hay (timothy), and feed her pellets in a percentage based on her weight (I'll refrain from giving the exact percentage I was told)!"

After that, I continued to take her in for health checkups every six months!

At 1 year and 10 months old, she started eating hay poorly, and when I took her back to the clinic, they found that her molars were sharp!

Since then, I've been taking her in every two months for teeth trimming!

This clinic was incredibly helpful because they would see us without an appointment, as long as it was within their operating hours.

One day, on a Sunday, my rabbit's teeth seemed to have become sharp, so I took her to the head veterinarian's clinic in Urawa!

The Urawa clinic was closed for the day.
This was the second time I'd gone on a Sunday and found it closed.
I couldn't wait until Monday, thinking, "Another day off?", so I called Bunny Grass, a hospital in Shibamata that I'd checked out before, and went there that day.
Thanks to them, my rabbit was able to live with me until January 2021, at 10 years and 5 months old.

Thank you to Saito Rabbit Clinic for your kind treatment and guidance, even though I was a novice rabbit owner.

However, the Sunday closures at the main Urawa clinic run by the head veterinarian are quite inconvenient for us owners (sweat...).

The photo is of my rabbit now!
I got him from a rabbit specialty shop in Shibamata.
His teeth are fine so far.
……………………………

"I usually record videos of my rabbits and parakeets, and my YouTube channel name is
Koichi's."

Since they specialize in rabbits, I have no doubts about the quality of their examinations regarding rabbit diseases and conditions. However, one of the two female veterinarians has a terrible attitude. I won't mention her name, but her tone is harsh and awful, and she comes across as cold. Even when I had questions, she gave off an unapproachable vibe. Her explanations weren't thorough, and she was completely condescending. I had nothing but an unpleasant experience.

I have my rabbit examined at this hospital every time. I've seen three different doctors so far, but Dr. Fukuura is dangerous.

He makes insensitive remarks (like saying the rabbit will die), has a condescending attitude, and blames pet owners.

When I took my family's rabbit in for an examination, I explained the circumstances and the number of days leading up to its illness, but he said, "You're being so vague, I can only give you a vague diagnosis. Can't you contact someone who knows more about this?" I was truly heartbroken.

From how he handles rabbits to how he interacts with owners, I feel no kindness or trustworthiness in anything he does.

The other doctors carefully examine each rabbit, communicate with them, and give individual attention, but Dr. Fukuura just says things like, "Some rabbits are like that," or "It's individual variation," and doesn't show any genuine concern.

There are many more things I could dig up, but having experienced the treatment from the other two doctors, Dr. Fukuura's careless and terrible treatment is particularly striking.

Please note that you cannot request a specific doctor at this hospital. If you wish to see the hospital director or Dr. Takaku, please be aware of this.

My child received care at this hospital for eight years.
As a foreigner, I sometimes had difficulty expressing my wishes in Japanese, but the head doctor always patiently (and empathetically) listened to me and carefully guided me on how to proceed.
Also, when I was unable to visit the hospital, Dr. Takaku gave me very kind advice over the phone, which was a great help.
A few years ago, when what we initially thought was plantar ulcer turned out to be cancer, they performed surgery, and my child's recovery was very smooth.
The fact that they performed non-surgical procedures (IVs, injections, etc.) in front of us was also very professional. For me, who tends to get nervous and anxious easily, that consideration gave me a great sense of security.
Sadly, Buibui-chan passed away, but I am filled with heartfelt gratitude to everyone at the hospital who cared for her so warmly over these eight years. Thank you so much.
